takeaway: Mean arterial pressure = [(2 × diastolic) + systolic]/3; diastole counts twice because two thirds of the cardiac cycle is diastole.

lines.text: Which value is two times the diastolic, plus the systolic, all divided by 3?
lines.say: Which value is two times the diastolic, plus the systolic, all divided by three?

lines.text: because two thirds of the cardiac cycle is spent in diastole.
Systolic pressure is counted once, and the total is divided by 3.
lines.say: Systolic pressure is counted once, and the total is divided by three.

lines.text: This gives the mean arterial pressure, or MAP.
lines.say: This gives the mean arterial pressure, or M A P.

lines.text: A MAP of 60 is needed to perfuse the coronary arteries, brain and kidneys; the reference range is 70 to 100 mmHg.
lines.say: An M A P of sixty is needed to perfuse the coronary arteries, brain and kidneys; the reference range is seventy to one hundred millimetres of mercury.

lines.text: So remember: MAP equals two diastolic plus one systolic, over 3.
lines.say: So remember: M A P equals two diastolic plus one systolic, over three.
